title: LoopCheck | Keep every change honest
narration: AI can change your web app in minutes. But checking that yesterday's features still work is repetitive. LoopCheck is an acceptance companion for solo builders using AI. It remembers the business behavior you approve and gives your coding tool reproducible evidence when a change breaks it.

title: Live Strands planning | Public MDN sample
narration: This is the real model path, using an unchanged public MDN shopping list. The goal asks for correct item text, a cleared input, and deletion. Strands and Qwen generate business requirements, then observe the page and propose executable checks. The operator reviews the exact expectations before approval. No preset check script is supplied on this path.

title: Recorded live tools | Failed attempts remain visible
narration: The recorded planning trace contains real page observations and a proposed binding. Earlier failures are retained in history. Planning is still bounded and can fail, including on a provider connection error. A model message alone cannot make an application pass.

title: Replay approved checks | No model request
narration: After approval, the same two flows run directly in Chromium. They check the actual item text, the cleared input and the empty list after deletion. Both pass on this source version. This ordinary replay uses no model request. Each run starts with a fresh browser context.

title: Cart workflow | Disclosed preset demonstration
narration: Now a separate cart walkthrough demonstrates the development cycle. Its requirements and code edits are scripted presets, clearly labeled in the interface. The browser checks are real. The baseline protects quantity changes, total calculation, invalid input and persistence.

title: Future behavior | Passing old checks is not enough
narration: We save a coupon requirement before its control exists: quantity two with SAVE10 must cost one hundred eighty. All three old flows still pass, but the new requirement has no check. LoopCheck correctly reports incomplete acceptance. The missing requirement cannot disappear behind a green result.

title: Injected regression | Expected 200, observed 300
narration: The demo script implements the coupon and deliberately introduces a price regression. The old quantity and persistence checks fail. Quantity two should cost two hundred, but the browser sees three hundred. The approved expected amount stays unchanged, and the result identifies this as a regression.

title: Evidence for the existing coding AI
narration: The full reproduction brief includes fresh-state prerequisites, every action, the failed assertion, expected and observed values, screenshots, versions and related files. A local MCP interface exposes prepare change, check change and get result. The coding AI changes the original project. MCP cannot approve or weaken the business requirements.

title: Repair and recheck | Same approved requirements
narration: Here the demo script restores the original price and keeps the coupon feature. All four flows pass on the repaired source. Historical results remain available, but only a current, fully covered, passing scope can approve the current change. No new model request is needed for this recheck.

title: Architecture and evaluation boundaries
narration: Strands plans and trial-runs checks. A separate browser verifier decides their results. SQLite keeps versioned requirements, evidence and cost reservations. The local edition connects trusted frontend projects; public mode accepts bundled samples only. Forty-eight automatic tests and twelve frozen mutation cases passed locally. These are engineering checks, not proof of production reliability or human time saved.

title: Try LoopCheck | Source and instructions on GitHub
narration: LoopCheck is MIT licensed and built with AI assistance. Try the disclosed keyless walkthrough, or configure the provider for live planning. This edited demonstration combines actual interface recordings and recorded planning evidence, with cuts between stages and synthetic narration. Source, installation instructions, retained failures and limitations are available in the public repository.
